# ui-compose

The compose box shared by chat buffers and the task board.

- **Runs in:** the UI (your Emacs)
- **Source:** [lisp/ui/harness-ui-compose.el](../../lisp/ui/harness-ui-compose.el)
- **Loaded:** by default
- **Requires:** [ui](ui.md)
- **Required by:** [ui-carry](ui-carry.md), [ui-pending](ui-pending.md), [ui-popout](ui-popout.md), [ui-sticky-compose](ui-sticky-compose.md), [ui-voice](ui-voice.md), [ui-workspace](ui-workspace.md)

## About

The editable box at the bottom of a chat buffer and of the task
board.  A host buffer calls `harness-compose-setup` once from its
major mode, then `harness-compose-insert` wherever it draws the box
(after making everything before it read-only).  The box gives:

  - multi-line editing: RET and C-j insert a newline, a placeholder
    shows while the box is empty;
  - replying to a quote: C-c > always replies in a thread, the same
    everywhere -- a card in the box for each region replied to, what
    it is and the part quoted, the reply typed under it.  No prefix
    argument quotes in the box instead.  A prompt is not a reply:
    `harness-prompt-region` in the box is the library's Markdown
    quote, where a quote can be split with M-RET and elided with
    C-c [ as [...];
  - replies in threads: a card in the box for each region replied to,
    what it is and the part of it quoted, with the words of the reply
    typed under it, in the same box (see the Threads section).  A
    reply with no region is a new thread: its card says so and has no
    quote, and the words under it start the thread on its own.  Your
    own message has a line above the first card, and C-c < moves
    point out of a reply to it, and back into the reply.  C-c e, or
    the card's menu, edits what the reply answers: trimmed, elided
    with [...], or split into replies of their own, each with its own
    card and words, as a mail answers a quote a part at a time (see
    Changing what a reply answers);
  - typing anywhere in the buffer goes into the box: a printable
    character (or a yank) with point outside it moves point to the
    end of the box and types there -- once the box holds a card, to
    the end of the area written in last, your message or a reply --
    unless the key is a command where it is typed -- a button's, a
    panel's, the task board's.  A command that acts on what is at
    point says where that is with a `harness-compose-acts-p`
    property; elsewhere its key types too;
  - the keys of the panels above the box from the box: a question's
    digits, a permission's y and n, the task board's F type when
    typed in the box, so C-c . shows the panel above the box and
    reads a key for it, pressing C-c . again going to the next panel
    up, point returning to the box (a numeric argument starts at the
    Nth panel up).  A host marks the text of a panel with a
    `harness-compose-panel` property, naming it, and says in its
    hints that C-c . is the way;
  - M-< and M-> go to the top and the bottom of the box, and on to
    those of the buffer from there (or with an argument, or outside
    the box);
  - a prompt that is a field of its own: C-a stops after it, as in
    the minibuffer, so C-a C-k clears the box's first line;
  - @file completion over the project's files, or over the file
    system for a path (/, ~/, ./, ../); each completed file becomes
    an attachment, its @ reference staying in the text, and so does
    the file an @ reference typed out in full names, once the message
    is sent; @task: completion over the project's tasks, the task
    chosen becoming an attachment; /skill completion at its start; a
    popup that shows as you type (corfu, company) shows for them even
    while the host redraws around the box;
  - the project's files of a chat working in a task's git worktree
    are those of the worktree and of the main checkout it was made
    from, which has what the worktree does not (untracked files, work
    not merged yet): the union of both, a file in both once, read
    from the worktree, and each marked with where it is, [task],
    [main] or [task, main] (`harness-compose-roots-function`);
  - attachments: C-c C-a finds a file the same way, by part of a
    project file's name or by path (C-u C-c C-a: browse the file
    system), or a task as task:ID (M-x harness-compose-attach-task
    reads one by its title), C-y pastes what the clipboard holds (an
    image or copied files go on the media ring; M-x
    harness-compose-attach-clipboard for other MIME types), files
    dropped on the window attach;
  - tokens: an attachment puts its token into the text where point
    is -- an image [image 1], a file @ and its path, a task
    @task:ID -- shown as a chip a click opens, so a sentence can name
    it; deleting the token removes the attachment (see the Tokens
    section);
  - the text and attachments, kept across redraws of the host;
  - long lines that wrap under the text, never scrolling sideways;
  - the attachments above the box, which a host draws with
    `harness-compose-insert-attachments`: one a line, each fitted to
    the narrowest window showing them (a long name shortened in the
    middle, its whole path in the tooltip) and fitted again when the
    windows change size;
  - optionally, the box at the bottom of the window: a buffer shorter
    than its window is padded at the top so it ends on the last line;
  - optionally, colours of its own: a host passes `:face` for the
    background and `:accent` for the prompt and a bar down the left
    edge, to mark a box that does something else than compose -- the
    task board's, which sends a message to a session.  It carries the
    bar onto its own lines around the box with `harness-compose-bar`.

Hosts read the box with `harness-compose-text` and
`harness-compose-take`, expand /skill references with
`harness-compose-with-expanded-text` and turn attachments into ACP
prompt blocks with `harness-compose-attachment-block`.
  - attachments: C-c C-a finds a project file by part of its name
  - links dropped from a web page download in the background, curl
  - yanking media: with `harness-compose-yank-media`, C-y attaches

## Provides

### Hooks

- `harness-compose-controls-functions` — Functions returning read-only control lines above a compose box.
- `harness-quote-target-functions` — Functions that say what C-c > quotes at point, or in a region.

### Commands

- `harness-compose-add-attachment` — Attach the file PATH (with MIME) to the next message.
- `harness-compose-attach-clipboard` — Attach what the clipboard holds.
- `harness-compose-attach-from-ring` — Attach an earlier capture of the media ring, chosen by name.
- `harness-compose-attach-task` — Attach TASK, a task of the box's project, to the next message.
- `harness-compose-beginning-of-buffer` — Move to the top of the compose box; from there, to the top of the buffer.
- `harness-compose-download` — Download URL in the background, then attach the file.
- `harness-compose-edit-thread` — Edit what a reply in a thread answers: trim it, elide it, or split it.
- `harness-compose-edit-thread-apply` — Put the quote the buffer holds back in the box, as the replies it makes.
- `harness-compose-edit-thread-cancel` — Leave the reply as it was; the quote the buffer holds goes.
- `harness-compose-edit-thread-elide` — Replace the region with `compose-quote-elision`, as a mail omits a part.
- `harness-compose-edit-thread-merge` — Join the reply at point with the one after it.
- `harness-compose-edit-thread-reset` — Start again from the quote as it was when this buffer opened.
- `harness-compose-edit-thread-split` — Split the quote at point into another reply.
- `harness-compose-end-of-buffer` — Move to the bottom of the compose box; from there, to the bottom of the buffer.
- `harness-compose-enter-reply` — Move point into a reply: to the end of the words under its card.
- `harness-compose-leave-reply` — Move point out of the reply, to your own message above the first card.
- `harness-compose-newline` — Insert a newline in the box, or jump there from elsewhere.
- `harness-compose-panel-key` — Press a key on a panel above the box, from the box.
- `harness-compose-remove-attachment` — Remove the attachment WHAT: a file's path, a task's task:ID, or itself.
- `harness-compose-toggle-reply` — Switch between your own message and the reply under a card.
- `harness-compose-yank` — Attach the image or the files on the clipboard, else yank text.
- `harness-compose-yank-pop` — Swap the media just yanked for an earlier capture of the media ring.
- `harness-quote-reply` — Reply to the quotable target at point, or to every target the region covers.

### Options

- `harness-compose-download-max-size` — Largest file, in bytes, that a link dropped on a compose box downloads.
- `harness-compose-reply-hints` — Non-nil: a card says how to move point out of its reply, and back in.
- `harness-compose-thumbnail-lines` — Height of the thumbnail an attached image or video shows, in lines.
- `harness-compose-yank-media` — Non-nil: yanking in a compose box attaches the media on the clipboard.
